corrections: Layer types are linear_attention for indices 0,1,2 and full_attention for 3,7,11,...; the earlier layer-2 label of full_attention was wrong (corrected in the PLE-stream receipt).
This work is RCO, a one-for-one expert replacement. No REAP mask or expert removal is produced.

host.gpu: GPU0, RTX 3090 Ti 24 GiB, shared with an unrelated Flint job using about 2.7 GiB
host.vm: win11-gaming stayed running; GPU1 was not needed or touched

method.boundary_handoff: pre-hook injection of the previous chunk's final hidden state
method.calibration: 1 sequence x 512 tokens (slice of the 256x2048 calibration matrix)
method.candidates: group-32 symmetric RTN at 4, 3, and 2 bits
method.output_sample: 8 experts per layer measured in output space
method.selection_signal: exact per-expert weight-space quantization error multiplied by the square root of routed token count

negative_result.resolution: Weighting the same error by routed token count raised the measured signal and cut the mean assembled error to 0.027626.
negative_result.statement: Selecting widths by weight-space error alone did not work: mean Spearman correlation against sampled per-expert output error was -0.003 over 144 samples, and the resulting 48-layer mean assembled error was 0.044624.

non_claims: One 512-token calibration sequence; not the 256x2048 recipe.
Per-layer reconstruction uses BF16 chunk inputs, not a fully cascaded quantized prefix.
Per-expert selection uses a measured proxy (weight error times routed load); only 8 experts per layer are checked in output space.
No end-to-end logits, served throughput, artifact packing, or engine run exists for this allocation.
scope: Full 48-layer quantization-aware RCO width allocation, one-for-one expert replacement
